One more thing: don't overmix the batter once you add the flour. Mix until just combined — overmixing develops too much gluten and creates a heavy, collapse-prone crumb. Try these fixes with your next batch and I bet it stays up.

conversation.content: Have you seen those stuffed tortilla videos where they put like cheese and meat inside a giant tortilla and fold it into a pocket? How do I actually make those?

Yes! Those are basically quesadilla pockets or 'tortilla wraps' depending on who's making them. The viral version usually uses a large flour tortilla with a cut from the center to one edge, then you fill four quadrants with different ingredients and fold them into a triangle. You need a burrito-size tortilla (the big ones), a sharp knife, and whatever fillings you want. Cut a straight line from the middle to the bottom edge — just one cut. Then imagine the tortilla in four sections.
Okay I think I've been cutting wrong because mine always fall apart. And what fillings work best?

The falling-apart issue is usually from overfilling — less is more with these. Put a THIN layer in each quadrant: bottom left could be seasoned rice, bottom right is shredded chicken, top right is cheese and sour cream, top left is pico de gallo or guac. Then fold: bottom left folds over to bottom right, then that folds up to top right, then over to top left. You end up with a neat triangle. Press it on a hot buttered skillet or griddle for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crispy.

Best combos: birria meat + cheese + consommé for dipping (incredible), breakfast version with scrambled eggs + bacon + cheese + avocado, or a dessert one with Nutella + strawberries + bananas. The key is keeping each layer thin so it actually folds and seals. Once the cheese melts it acts like glue holding everything together. Your kids will go crazy for these.

Season it right, cook it slow, and a cheaper cut will give you 90% of the oxtail experience at a fraction of the price.
